messages:
anita: heads up — ran the new reranker build (bert-ranker-3q-ptq) on a prod-sampled eval. seeing NDCG@10 down ~1.8% vs fp16 baseline, MRR roughly flat. quick triage please.

sam: how big is the sample? and are you doing CI/bootstrap?

anita: 50k queries from prod logs (last 7 days), stratified by query freq. bootstrap 1000 resamples -> ndcg drop CI [-2.6%, -0.9%].

matt: did you hold the doc pool constant? i.e., retrieval identical?

anita: yes — same topK=100 from retrieval. only reranker weights changed (post-PTQ 4-bit). baseline was fp16.

lucy: tiny flag — did tokenization/normalization change in preprocessing recently? we merged whitespace normalizer last week.

anita: good catch. i ran an ablation: using the old normalizer reduces the ndcg gap by ~50%. so formatting change interacts with quantization.

sam: can you paste the eval command you used?

anita: ```./eval_runner --model reranker-ptq-4bit --queries queries.jsonl --qdocs topk.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --bootstrap 1000 --seed 42```

matt: breakdown by query segments? long tail vs head?

anita: yep. freq quartiles: Q1 (tail) ndcg -3.5%, Q2 -1.9%, Q3 -1.0%, Q4 (head) +0.2%. so tail queries get hurt most by PTQ.

lucy: we should compute per-query rank deltas and inspect some failing pairs to see if tokenization differences change ranking order.

anita: uploaded a small repro set to gs://redwood-evals/reranker/1767129999/repro.jsonl (10k queries + topk).

sam: thinking aloud — maybe calibrate logits after PTQ (temperature scaling) or a tiny bias correction could help. also try dynamic int8 rather than static 4-bit PTQ.

matt: stats check — run paired bootstrap + Wilcoxon signed-rank for nonparametric confirmation.

anita: did both. paired bootstrap p~0.004; wilcoxon p~0.007 for overall ndcg@10. significant.

lucy: schedule experiments: ptq-4bit-static (current), int8-dynamic, fp16-ref. also run with old normalizer vs new normalizer as cross-factor.

anita: kicking off eval jobs now — eval-bot: queued 3 jobs (ptq4-static, int8-dynamic, fp16-ref) ids 9891,9892,9893.

eval-bot: job 9891 completed: ndcg@10 delta -1.77% CI [-2.6, -0.94], p=0.004.

eval-bot: job 9892 completed: ndcg@10 delta -0.30% CI [-0.9, +0.2], p=0.12.

sam: int8-dynamic looks promising — smaller quality loss and likely better perf than fp16 cost ratio. can we run a small % live canary?

matt: yes but document rollback path and monitor top-k drift and latency p95.

anita: latency stable within 4% p95, cost ~35% lower for int8 pipeline. i'll prepare canary config and PR.

lucy: please include a standardized eval artifact in the PR: per-query delta CSV, seed, commands, and the exact tokenization config. that will avoid future surprises.

anita: will add artifact + reproducible seed + a short script to reproduce locally. thanks all :thumbsup:
